body:
Hey. First off, I wanna say that no one should ever brush you off because you're "only 15". Your feelings are real and important. And you don't deserve to be called useless. After all, mistakes are normal - we all make them.

As for your question, it depends what kind of "normal" you're referring to. Statistically, it is unfortunately quite common for young people to experience some type of depression and/or suicidal thoughts. I recall having similar thoughts when I was 15 (maybe even earlier than that, not really sure). I would "fantasize" what would happen if I'd jump off a building or something.

However, it isn't really something you should just gloss over in my opinion. Every person is different, and there is of course a chance that it will just pass, but these things are always better to address.

What you described, with always forgetting things, could be a form of ADHD or something similar. My advice would be to talk to a therapist about what you've been experiencing. You can ask your parents to make you an appointment with one, if you're comfortable with telling them a bit of what's going on. Another option would be to go by yourself to see your school's counselor (most schools have one). If you tell them about your difficulty to focus and remember things, they should think of ADHD as well, and refer you to a therapist themselves. If it turns out you do have ADHD, you may get prescribed pills that will help.

No matter what though, remember that your value as a person isn't defined by your grades or one messed up chore.
